chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed tawaf around the House but did not know whether he had performed six circuits or seven circuits of the obligatory tawaf. He said, 'Let him repeat his tawaf.' It was said to him, 'He has already left and that time has passed.' He said, 'There is no penalty upon him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no penalty/dam upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim is unsure whether they completed six or seven circuits of tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and ease in Shia jurisprudence, where uncertainty in ritual acts is resolved by requiring a repeat for certainty unless practical constraints, such as the departure time for Hajj, make it burdensome. The Imam’s ruling highlights the distinction between the obligatory *tawaf al-fad* (seven circuits) and the flexibility granted when doubt arises just before the pilgrim's scheduled departure, reflecting the Shia emphasis on removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in worship.
